root_cause_label: Plain nested-loop C implementation without BLAS, producing only ~1.1x speedup instead of required 1.2x, followed by marginal micro-optimizations that never bridged the gap
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented an O(n²) nested-loop C extension that achieved at best ~1.1x speedup instead of the required 1.2x, and spent the remainder of the trajectory in a repetitive cycle of failed micro-optimizations (restrict, pragma ivdep, symmetry exploitation) rather than adopting a fundamentally stronger strategy such as BLAS/cblas_dsymv.
t_err_evidence: Step 8: Agent implements portfolio_risk_c using plain nested O(n²) loops without BLAS or any vectorized library call. This is the decisive mistake: the approach will never reliably achieve 1.2x over a pure-Python O(n²) loop at large N, where the overhead difference is minimal compared to the computation.
t_commit_evidence: Step 20: After the first benchmark (step 17) showed 1.1x speedup, the agent's response is to try loop fusion (fused single loop vs two-loop), which is a marginal tweak. From step 20 onward, all subsequent actions are minor variants of the same micro-optimization pattern. The agent never attempts BLAS or a fundamentally different algorithm, locking in the failing trajectory.
t_surface_evidence: Step 17: First full benchmark run shows 'Speedup: 1.1x' and 'Performance requirement NOT met (1.1x < 1.2x)' for N=5000, and the N=8000 test hangs/times out.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked the domain/API knowledge that achieving a reliable 1.2x+ speedup over a pure-Python O(n²) loop requires more than a naive C port with compiler flags. Using cblas_dsymv or numpy's optimized BLAS-backed matrix-vector multiply would have provided the necessary speedup. Instead, the agent applied only surface-level optimizations (loop fusion, restrict, pragma ivdep, symmetry) that never produced consistent 1.2x speedup at N=5000.
forewarning_evidence: Step 17: Benchmark reports 1.1x speedup (below 1.2x requirement) and the N=8000 test hangs indefinitely, clearly signaling that the approach was insufficient.
